updates.title: Claude Haiku 5.5: new default small model (breaking change)
updates.what_changed: claude-haiku-5-5 is now the default Haiku model. Adaptive thinking is on by default. Manual extended thinking via budget_tokens now returns a 400 error, which breaks existing integrations.
updates.how_it_works: 1M token context, 128k max output, $0.10/$0.50 per Mtok (standard). Pass thinking:{type:'disabled'} to turn off adaptive thinking. budget_tokens is rejected outright; migrate to the effort parameter.
updates.how_to_get: Model ID: claude-haiku-5-5. Available on Claude API, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud and Microsoft Foundry. A migration guide is in the platform docs.
updates.impact: Any Claude API agent using a Haiku model with manual budget_tokens will throw 400 errors. Audit agent code before the next deployment.
updates.action: Search agent code for budget_tokens and replace it with the adaptive thinking effort parameter, or temporarily pin the old model while testing.

updates.title: Sonnet 5.5 prompt cache read price halved
updates.what_changed: Claude Sonnet 5.5 cache read price drops from $0.20 to $0.10 per million tokens, now 0.05× the base input price. Cache write prices are unchanged.
updates.how_it_works: Savings apply automatically to all cached Sonnet 5.5 API requests. No code or config changes are required.
updates.how_to_get: Applies automatically to existing Sonnet 5.5 API calls that use prompt caching. No opt-in needed.
updates.impact: Direct cost reduction for Claude API pipelines using Sonnet 5.5 with prompt caching. It could be significant for high-volume agentic workflows.
updates.action: Pull last month's cache-read token spend, project the savings and update your cost models and delivery estimates.

updates.title: Managed Agents: web_fetch restricted to prior-context URLs
updates.what_changed: web_fetch in Claude Managed Agents now only fetches URLs that appeared in prior session context. URLs present only in Claude's output, system prompt or tool output return a url_not_in_prior_context error.
updates.how_it_works: A server-side security control that reduces data exfiltration risk. It is enforced automatically in all Managed Agent environments; no configuration is needed.
updates.how_to_get: Applies automatically to all Managed Agent environments. There is no opt-in. Review agent designs that pass URLs only via system prompt or tool results.
updates.impact: Managed Agent workflows that build URLs dynamically and pass them only via system prompt or tool output will break, so an architecture review is needed.
updates.action: Test every Managed Agent pipeline using web_fetch to confirm target URLs appear in prior user-turn or assistant-turn context before being fetched.

updates.title: SDK toolsets for browser and computer use (Beta)
updates.what_changed: The Python and TypeScript Anthropic SDKs now include typed classes for browser use and computer use tools. Subclass and implement one method per tool; the SDK handles the tool loop and policies automatically.
updates.how_it_works: Subclass BrowserTool or ComputerTool, implement the action method and pass it to the agent. The SDK manages retry logic, tool-call parsing and safety policies.
updates.how_to_get: Beta. Use the latest Anthropic Python or TypeScript SDK. See the browser-use-sdk documentation in the Claude platform docs.
updates.impact: Reduces boilerplate when building browser-automation or computer-use agents. Worth evaluating for upcoming web-scraping or UI-automation agent builds.
updates.action: Spike the browser-use toolset on a non-production Claude API project and compare the effort against a manual tool-loop approach.

updates.title: Claude Code v2.1.293–295 patch bundle (07–08 Oct)
updates.what_changed: Three releases: Haiku 5.5 is the default Haiku model in Claude Code; onFailure:'block' added to command/HTTP hooks; remote MCP reconnection fixed after 15s+ outages; context compaction no longer wrongly marks actions complete; 150+ other fixes.
updates.how_it_works: onFailure:'block' on a hook stops the current operation when the hook fails. Remote MCP servers now reconnect automatically with exponential backoff after drops. Update via claude --version / auto-update.
updates.how_to_get: Update Claude Code to v2.1.295. No additional config changes are needed for most fixes.
updates.impact: More reliable agent execution. Hook-based guards are stronger, and remote MCP outage recovery reduces the need for manual session restarts.
updates.action: Run claude --version, update to v2.1.295 on all dev machines, and update hooks to use onFailure:'block' where guard behaviour is required.

updates.title: Deprecation: old file picker, Desktop March 2026 or earlier loses OneDrive/SharePoint save
updates.what_changed: From October 2026, Power BI Desktop versions from March 2026 or earlier can no longer save or share .pbix files to OneDrive and SharePoint. The old file picker is removed for those versions.
updates.how_it_works: Users on old Desktop builds silently lose OneDrive/SharePoint save until they upgrade. There is no workaround; updating is the only fix.
updates.how_to_get: Update Power BI Desktop to April 2026 or later to keep OneDrive/SharePoint save functionality.
updates.impact: Anyone on an outdated Desktop version will silently lose the ability to save reports to OneDrive/SharePoint, a workflow-breaking change for Power BI teams.
updates.action: Audit Desktop versions across your team and report authors, and enforce an update to April 2026 or later Desktop now.

updates.title: Power BI Agentic Experiences (GA)
updates.what_changed: AI agents can now build and modify Power BI semantic models and reports end-to-end using the powerbi-authoring plugin in microsoft/skills-for-fabric, MCP tools and Power BI Desktop Bridge. Remote semantic models and more visual types, including custom visuals, are supported.
updates.how_it_works: Point an agent at a requirements doc or layout screenshot. It reads and writes models and reports via MCP, then reloads changes in Desktop or validates via headless browser. Desktop isn't required for Mac or remote workflows.
updates.how_to_get: GA. Use the powerbi-authoring plugin from microsoft/skills-for-fabric with a compatible MCP client (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot App). See the Power BI agentic documentation.
updates.impact: Agents can handle the initial Power BI authoring pass while humans review and refine, cutting developer time per report.
updates.action: Set up the powerbi-authoring plugin with Claude Code and pilot agent-driven report creation in a non-production workspace.

updates.title: Remote Power BI Authoring MCP Server (Preview)
updates.what_changed: A cloud-hosted MCP server lets AI agents create and modify Fabric semantic models with no local installation, which unblocks Mac and Linux users. Endpoint: https://api.fabric.microsoft.com/v1/mcp/powerbi/authoring
updates.how_it_works: Any MCP client authenticates via Entra ID to the remote endpoint. It has the same authoring capabilities as the local server and is recommended for Direct Lake semantic model creation in Fabric workspaces.
updates.how_to_get: Preview. Configure the remote MCP endpoint in your MCP client config. Requires Fabric workspace access and Entra ID auth.
updates.impact: Claude Code and Claude API agents can create and modify Fabric semantic models in CI/CD pipelines with no local Desktop dependency, which is critical for headless automation.
updates.action: Add the remote MCP endpoint to Claude Code's MCP server config and test semantic model creation in a dev Fabric workspace.

updates.title: Power BI Projects (PBIP) GA: PBIR is now the default report format
updates.what_changed: PBIP is now GA. Power BI Enhanced Report Format (PBIR) is the new default for all PBIX and PBIP files, and TMDL is the default for semantic models. Existing reports auto-convert to PBIR when edited in Power BI tools.
updates.how_it_works: New reports use PBIR from creation, and editing a legacy-format report triggers automatic conversion. PBIP stores definitions as human-readable text, enabling Git diffs, PR reviews, CI/CD automation and agent-driven edits.
updates.how_to_get: GA. Available in current Power BI Desktop and service. No opt-in required. Existing PBIX files convert to PBIR on next edit.
updates.impact: Power BI repos should adopt PBIP/PBIR. CI/CD pipelines that handle PBIX binary files need updating for the new directory-based PBIR format.
updates.action: Review pipelines for PBIX binary handling, migrate active repos to PBIP and validate build/release steps against the PBIR file structure.

updates.title: New governance control for Copilot access to semantic models
updates.what_changed: Semantic model editors can now block read-only users from accessing the model through Copilot and Microsoft's remote MCP tools. This covers PBI Copilot, M365 Copilot Chat/Cowork, data agents and Fabric/PBI MCP servers.
updates.how_it_works: A new per-model setting in the Copilot section: 'Allow any person with read-only access to use AI on the model.' It is enabled by default. Editors disable it per model to restrict AI access to editors only.
updates.how_to_get: Available now in the Power BI service. Requires semantic model write permission to configure.
updates.impact: Organizations with sensitive or regulated semantic models can enforce AI access controls independently of standard read permissions, which matters for financial or healthcare data.
updates.action: Review sensitive semantic models across your workspaces and configure the AI access setting to restrict Copilot access where governance requires it.

updates.title: APPROXIMATEDISTINCTCOUNT extended to Import and Direct Lake (Preview)
updates.what_changed: The DAX function APPROXIMATEDISTINCTCOUNT, previously only for DirectQuery sources, now works on Import and Direct Lake semantic models, including Direct Lake on OneLake and Direct Lake on SQL.
updates.how_it_works: It estimates unique value counts with ~1.6% standard error using a fast probabilistic approach. It is significantly faster than DISTINCTCOUNT on high-cardinality columns, with millions of unique values like transaction IDs or user IDs.
updates.how_to_get: Preview. Use APPROXIMATEDISTINCTCOUNT(<columnName>) in DAX on any Import or Direct Lake model. No version or SKU requirement beyond standard Power BI.
updates.impact: Can speed up slow reports on large Fabric Lakehouse or Direct Lake models where high-cardinality distinct counts are the bottleneck.
updates.action: Find your slowest DISTINCTCOUNT measures, swap in APPROXIMATEDISTINCTCOUNT in a dev model and benchmark the query time improvement.

updates.title: Microsoft 365 Copilot integrated into Power BI (Preview)
updates.what_changed: M365 Copilot is now available as an embedded pane inside Power BI and Fabric. Shared conversation history carries across M365 experiences. It combines Fabric IQ data answers with Work IQ context (emails, meetings, documents).
updates.how_it_works: An admin enables it in the Fabric admin portal (off by default). It requires an M365 Copilot licence per user. It is independent of the standalone Power BI Copilot setting, so both can coexist.
updates.how_to_get: Preview. An M365 Copilot licence is required, and a Fabric admin must enable the entry point in the admin portal.
updates.impact: Organizations with M365 Copilot licences can query Power BI data alongside M365 work context from a single pane inside Power BI.
updates.action: Identify which environments have M365 Copilot licences and plan a pilot for one workspace after reviewing the admin toggle and governance implications.

updates.title: DirectQuery semantic models now editable in Power BI service (GA)
updates.what_changed: DirectQuery semantic models can now be created and edited directly in the Power BI service without Power BI Desktop. You get full in-browser modeling control: connect to a DQ source, manage relationships, write DAX and switch storage modes. Composite models are also available on the web.
updates.how_it_works: Open an existing DQ model or create a new one in the Power BI service. Real-time collaboration is supported. Works on Mac, Linux and Windows.
updates.how_to_get: GA. Available in the Power BI service to users with semantic model write permission. No additional licence required.
updates.impact: Mac and Linux users can now author DirectQuery semantic models in the browser without needing a Windows VM for Power BI Desktop.
updates.action: Test web-based DirectQuery model authoring in a non-production Fabric workspace and document how the workflow differs from Desktop.

updates.title: Planning in Fabric: Native Engine, event triggers and Fabric IQ writeback
updates.what_changed: Three new capabilities: (1) Native Planning Engine built on Rust/Apache Arrow, up to 10× performance at tens of millions of cells (Preview); (2) event triggers start pipelines, Dataflow Gen2, notebooks and Teams/email on writeback events; (3) streamlined writeback to the source semantic model so Copilot and data agents reason over actuals plus plan.
updates.how_it_works: Event triggers fire when a writeback starts, succeeds or fails, passing execution metadata as parameters to downstream Fabric items. Writeback adds plan tables to the semantic model, giving Fabric IQ agents forward-looking context.
updates.how_to_get: Fabric IQ Planning (GA since July 2026). Native Engine and some trigger capabilities are in Preview. Requires Fabric capacity with a Planning licence (Planner/Stakeholder sessions).
updates.impact: For teams on Fabric Planning, event triggers can automate downstream pipeline orchestration, removing manual handoffs between planning cycles and data refresh jobs.
updates.action: Prototype an event trigger linking a writeback-succeeded event to a pipeline or Dataflow Gen2 run in a sandbox workspace.

updates.title: Fabric Core MCP Server (GA)
updates.what_changed: The cloud-hosted MCP server for Fabric is now GA. Any MCP client authenticated via Entra ID can search the OneLake catalog, manage workspaces, items, folders and permissions, and view capacity info, with no local installation.
updates.how_it_works: Standard MCP protocol over HTTPS to a remote Fabric endpoint. All operations respect Fabric RBAC and are recorded in Fabric audit logs. No custom integration is required.
updates.how_to_get: GA. Configure the Fabric Core MCP endpoint in any compatible MCP client (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot App). Entra ID authentication is required. See the Fabric Core MCP Server documentation.
updates.impact: Claude Code and Claude API agents can now automate Fabric workspace management, item deployment and permission changes, supporting AI-driven data engineering delivery.
updates.action: Add the Fabric Core MCP endpoint to Claude Code's MCP server config and test workspace listing, item discovery and permission queries in a dev Fabric environment.

updates.title: Agentic Fabric notebook development: FNTK + Claude Code VS Code integration (Preview)
updates.what_changed: Two features: (1) the Fabric Notebook Toolkit (FNTK) Python library gives Claude Code, Codex and Copilot CLI a safe command surface for notebook discovery, authoring, targeted cell editing, remote execution and diagnostics; (2) the Fabric DE VS Code extension exposes a local MCP server so Claude Code can retrieve active notebook context (language, workspace, runtime, Lakehouse, selected cell) before generating code.
updates.how_it_works: FNTK closes the gap between code generation and a completed notebook outcome. The VS Code MCP server lets Claude Code fetch notebook context on demand; generated code is previewed in the extension and the developer accepts or rejects it before any change is applied.
updates.how_to_get: Preview. Install the FNTK Python library, update the Fabric DE VS Code extension to the latest version and enable Claude Code integration via the VS Code command palette. Requires the Claude Code VS Code extension.
updates.impact: Turns Claude Code from a Spark code generator into a full Fabric notebook development agent, end-to-end without copy-paste.
updates.action: Install FNTK and enable the Fabric DE VS Code Claude Code integration on active notebook projects; pilot a complete end-to-end notebook authoring loop.

updates.title: Project Osmos: autonomous agentic Data Engineering (Preview)
updates.what_changed: An agentic DE experience in Fabric where you define the desired outcome and guardrails, and Osmos autonomously inspects the workspace, plans work, writes and runs Spark, creates or updates Fabric items and validates results, handling project-scale DE initiatives without manual steps.
updates.how_it_works: Delegate a Task with guardrails. Osmos maps workspace context, designs for reuse, writes maintainable Spark, then tests and refines. Tasks persist across sessions and multiple agents explore approaches in parallel. Authorized team members can steer the same Task from Fabric or coding-agent surfaces.
updates.how_to_get: Preview. Access via Fabric Data Engineering. Requires Fabric capacity with appropriate permissions. See Data Engineering in Microsoft Fabric documentation.
updates.impact: High potential to accelerate DE delivery, possibly handling Lakehouse migration, ETL modernization and platform setup tasks within Fabric.
updates.action: Sign up for the Project Osmos Preview and pilot it on a single contained DE task, such as one ETL notebook migration, in a sandbox workspace.

updates.title: Fabric CI/CD Deployment Plan (Preview)
updates.what_changed: A new Deployment Plan Fabric item gives explicit, ordered control over multi-item deployments via a visual canvas. Arrange items in ordered sets and add pre/post actions (notebooks, pipelines, copy jobs, Dataflow Gen2, UDFs). The plan stops on failure before dependent items proceed.
updates.how_it_works: Create a Deployment Plan item in a Git-connected workspace. Define ordered deployment sets and inter-set actions on a canvas. Works with both Git integration and deployment pipelines, and handles dependencies Fabric cannot auto-detect.
updates.how_to_get: Preview. Create a Deployment Plan item in any Fabric workspace connected to Git. See the Plan CI/CD for Microsoft Fabric Solutions documentation.
updates.impact: Improves Fabric CI/CD with predictable, dependency-aware deployment ordering, with data prep and validation steps built in as first-class actions.
updates.action: Design a Deployment Plan for your most complex Fabric workspace and test ordered deployment with a pre-action notebook in a dev environment.

updates.title: Bulk Export/Import API (GA) + fabric-cicd dynamic replacement
updates.what_changed: The Bulk Export/Import Item Definitions APIs are now GA (removed from the beta path). The open-source fabric-cicd tool's bulk option is production-ready and now supports dynamic replacement, resolving environment-specific values (connection strings, workspace IDs) at deploy time.
updates.how_it_works: One API call exports or imports all item definitions from or to a workspace. Dynamic replacement resolves per-environment variables in item definitions during deployment, so environment-specific config no longer needs hardcoding in Fabric items.
updates.how_to_get: GA. Use the Fabric Core REST API, or update the fabric-cicd CLI to the latest version for dynamic replacement. See the fabric-cicd Bulk Option documentation.
updates.impact: Closes a major gap in Fabric CI/CD across dev/test/prod. Connection strings and workspace IDs no longer need hardcoding per environment.
updates.action: Update fabric-cicd to the latest version and configure dynamic replacement for connection strings and workspace IDs across your Fabric deployment pipelines.

updates.title: Fabric IQ MCP Server (GA)
updates.what_changed: The Fabric IQ MCP server is now GA. MCP-compatible AI clients and agents can discover Power BI reports and semantic models, inspect their metadata, search for business data and execute DAX queries against authorized semantic models, all via a standardized MCP endpoint.
updates.how_it_works: AI applications connect via MCP to the Fabric IQ endpoint (svc.cloud.microsoft domain). Existing Fabric permissions, RLS and OLS are enforced. Versioned tool contracts support stable integrations. Future expansion to ontologies and data agents is planned.
updates.how_to_get: GA. Configure the Fabric IQ MCP endpoint in any compatible MCP client. Requires Fabric workspace access with appropriate semantic model read permissions.
updates.impact: Claude API agents can now query and reason over Power BI semantic models as part of automated analytics pipelines, enabling AI-driven insight delivery.
updates.action: Add Fabric IQ MCP to Claude Code's MCP config, test DAX query execution against a non-production semantic model and evaluate it for analytics agent builds.

updates.title: Mirroring for Google BigQuery (GA)
updates.what_changed: Fabric Mirroring from Google BigQuery is now Generally Available. It enables near-real-time replication of BigQuery data into OneLake in Delta format, queryable via Fabric Lakehouse, Warehouse, Power BI Direct Lake and other Fabric experiences.
updates.how_it_works: Configure via Fabric Data Factory Mirroring. BigQuery data is continuously replicated into OneLake as Delta Parquet, making it available across Fabric without custom ETL pipelines.
updates.how_to_get: GA. Configure via Fabric Data Factory Mirroring. Requires BigQuery source access credentials and appropriate Fabric capacity.
updates.impact: Teams running BigQuery can mirror data into Fabric for cross-cloud reporting or integration scenarios without duplicating dbt pipeline logic.
updates.action: If you run BigQuery alongside Fabric, assess whether mirroring could support cross-cloud reporting or Fabric-side analytical requirements.

updates.title: Custom Live Pools for Fabric Data Engineering (GA)
updates.what_changed: Custom live pools keep Spark clusters pre-warmed on a defined schedule, with custom libraries pre-installed via Fabric environments. Notebook sessions start in approximately 5 seconds. Pool configs and schedules are now manageable via public APIs.
updates.how_it_works: Configure a custom Spark pool with a Fabric environment using Full publishing mode. Define a warm-up schedule and number of warm clusters. Pools scale proportionally as capacity scales. API support enables automated pool management in CI/CD.
updates.how_to_get: GA. Requires paid Fabric capacity (Trial and Starter Pools not supported). Configure via Fabric workspace settings or the public pool management APIs.
updates.impact: Eliminates Spark cold-start delays for Fabric notebook workloads, valuable for interactive exploration and time-sensitive scheduled pipeline runs.
updates.action: Identify your highest-frequency Fabric notebook workloads and configure a custom live pool with the required libraries and a warm-up schedule matching usage patterns.
